titleEn: Growers Share Lessons and Wins in Automation
titleZh: 种植者分享自动化转型的经验与成果
summaryZh: 本文报道了Cultivate'26展会上三位园艺种植者（来自苗圃、农场和种苗公司）关于自动化实施的真实经验分享。他们讨论了决定自动化的时机、优先级选择、团队适应、设备切换管理、制造商关系以及投资回报率衡量等关键问题。文章提供了从预算、文化转变到实际ROI对比的实用教训，对智慧畜牧行业在自动化决策、员工培训和效益评估方面具有跨领域参考价值。
featuredReason: 虽然本文聚焦于园艺温室，但其中关于自动化决策、团队文化转变、ROI衡量及设备切换管理的经验，对智慧畜牧行业（如养殖场自动化升级）具有高度可迁移的实践参考价值。
contentFull:
By Brian D. Sparks|July 23, 2026 

 

 

 

 The shift to automation works different for almost any greenhouse operation, but when done right, this shift should involve a few common themes: budget and ROI considerations, workflow changes, and training/implementation.

 During Cultivate’26, a panel featuring three growers featured candid, practical lessons on automation implementation in real operations. The group shared how they approached training and culture shifts, mistakes they would avoid next time, and how actual ROI compared to projections.

 The panel included:

 Brian Groves, Commercial Lead, Ornamentals at AdeptAg (moderator)

 Mike Miller, General Manager and CEO of Decker’s Nursery in Ohio

 Joseph Capps, Operations Manager at Worthington Farms in North Carolina

 Casey Stanton, Production Manager at Raker-Roberta’s Young Plants in Michigan

 Keep reading for an overview of some of the questions raised during the discussion, and insights shared by each panelist.

 When did you decide that automation was necessary at your operation?

 Miller: “During the recession, we noticed that our sales numbers were hiding a lot of internal errors. We also knew we didn’t want to be the same business we’d always been.”

 Capps: “We added a production line that produced smaller plants. This shortened our production timeline, so we needed to become more efficient for the betterment of our business and our team.”

 Stanton: “For us, it was not one singular decision. We made automation a part of our culture and looked at all of our processes so we could identify any bottlenecks that were preventing us from becoming more efficient.”

 How did you decide what to prioritize?

 Capps: “We knew we couldn’t produce plants faster with the equipment we had, so we focused on updating our potting equipment for smaller pots. This also gave us a chance to take our crews to other operations and see how they were using new equipment.”

 How has automation played out with your team?

 Miller: “Once we made the shift, our team quickly learned how their jobs would become easier.”

 Capps: “We were able to run the machines in less time than I thought. Our employees became really interested in learning how to use them.”

 Stanton: “We were surprised at how quickly some of our employees stepped up and wanted to learn more. Our success comes from a mix of top-down and bottom-up ideas, and we encourage our team to suggest better ways of doing things.”

 How do you manage the change-over process to a new piece of equipment?

 Miller: “Through communication and follow up. We trust that our team will eventually manage the process themselves.”

 Capps: “We try to highlight both the day-to-day and the long-term, big picture benefits.”

 Stanton: “We started using a live dashboard to show efficiency gains in real time.”

 How important is your relationship with the manufacturer?

 Miller: “We’re close in proximity to the main company we work with. That nearby technical support is critical as equipment gets older.”

 Stanton: “It can be very important. We want to make sure there’s consistency in the technology we’re using so that when we choose to upgrade, the process will be easier.”

 How do you measure return on investment?

 Miller: “You have to build profitability into your costs, and you have to measure as much as you can. Also, don’t just go with the shiny new piece of equipment. There’s a lot of smaller, less expensive options that can make a big difference.”

 Capps: “Don’t look at where you are now as a company. Look at the numbers for where you want to be five years from now.”

translationZh:
对于几乎任何温室运营来说，向自动化的转型方式各不相同，但如果做得好，这种转型应该涉及几个共同主题：预算与投资回报率考量、工作流程变化以及培训/实施。

在Cultivate'26展会上，一个由三位种植者组成的小组分享了在真实运营中实施自动化的坦诚而实用的经验。他们讨论了如何应对培训和文化的转变、下次会避免哪些错误，以及实际投资回报率与预期的对比情况。

小组成员包括：

Brian Groves，AdeptAg观赏植物商业负责人（主持人）

Mike Miller，俄亥俄州Decker's Nursery总经理兼首席执行官

Joseph Capps，北卡罗来纳州Worthington Farms运营经理

Casey Stanton，密歇根州Raker-Roberta's Young Plants生产经理

请继续阅读以下内容，了解讨论中提出的一些问题以及每位小组成员分享的见解。

**您是什么时候决定在运营中必须引入自动化的？**

Miller：“在经济衰退期间，我们注意到销售额掩盖了许多内部错误。我们也知道，我们不想成为一成不变的企业。”

Capps：“我们增加了一条生产小规格植物的生产线。这缩短了我们的生产周期，因此我们需要提高效率，以利于我们的业务和团队。”

Stanton：“对我们来说，这不是一个单一的决策。我们将自动化融入我们的文化，审视所有流程，以便找出阻碍我们提高效率的瓶颈。”

**您如何决定优先考虑什么？**

Capps：“我们知道，用现有设备无法更快地生产植物，因此我们专注于更新用于小盆的装盆设备。这也让我们有机会带领团队参观其他运营场所，看看他们是如何使用新设备的。”

**自动化在您的团队中效果如何？**

Miller：“一旦我们做出转变，我们的团队很快就了解到他们的工作将如何变得更轻松。”

Capps：“我们能够比我预想的更短的时间内运行这些机器。我们的员工对学习如何使用它们变得非常感兴趣。”

Stanton：“我们惊讶于一些员工如此迅速地站出来，想要学习更多。我们的成功来自于自上而下和自下而上的想法相结合，我们鼓励团队提出更好的工作方法。”

**您如何管理新设备的切换过程？**

Miller：“通过沟通和跟进。我们相信，团队最终会自己管理这个过程。”

Capps：“我们努力强调日常效益和长期的大局利益。”

Stanton：“我们开始使用实时仪表板来展示效率提升。”

**您与制造商的关系有多重要？**

Miller：“我们与主要合作的公司地理位置很近。随着设备老化，附近的技术支持至关重要。”

Stanton：“这可能非常重要。我们希望确保所使用的技术具有一致性，这样当我们选择升级时，过程会更顺利。”

**您如何衡量投资回报率？**

Miller：“你必须将盈利能力纳入成本考量，并且要尽可能多地衡量。另外，不要只盯着闪亮的新设备。有很多更小、更便宜的选择也能带来巨大改变。”

Capps：“不要只看公司现在的状况。要着眼于五年后你希望达到的数字。”
